newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain reports attack on consul's house in Havana.
newsitem.headline: Spain reports attack on consul's house in Havana.

text.p: Unidentified assailants have vandalised the house of the Spanish consul in Havana, the Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday, as tension mounted between the two countries over the appointment of a new Spanish ambassador.

A senior ministry official held out the possibility of reprisals, including the expulsion of Cuba's ambassador, after the attack on Monday night following Cuba's retraction last week of its earlier approval for a new Spanish ambassador to Havana.
"The house of the Spanish consul in Havana has been attacked last night," the official told Reuters.
The assailants punctured the tyres of consul Eduardo Cerro's car and stole a television antenna, a ministry spokesman said. No further details were immediately available.

Relations between Spain and Cuba have deteriorated to their lowest point in years after Havana accused Madrid last week of meddling in its affairs by urging the European Union to adopt a tougher policy towards Havana in a push for democratic reforms in the communist state.

The official said the government was not ruling out countermeasures, including the expulsion of Cuba's ambassador, in retaliation for Monday's attack and the cancellation of a planned Spanish book exhibit and conference in Havana.
"We can name a new ambassador (to Cuba) or not. We can have this woman here or not," said the official, referring to Cuba's ambassador to Spain, Rosario Navas.
Foreign Ministry officials said on Monday Spain might take several months to name a replacement ambassador to Cuba, and would only do so after Havana indicated it would approve the new candidate.
The incident at the consul's residence came days after Spain asked Cuba to protect its embassy for fear of attacks.
Cuban authorities placed a security cordon around the embassy, posting hundreds of police and plain-clothes guards outside to head off any disturbances.
The new Spanish government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar has adopted a much tougher line in pressing for democratic reform in Cuba than its Socialist predecessor.
